title: Excavating Joysagar: an interpretation
period: Rangpur area, Rudra Singha’s reign, circa 1696–1714
scene: Expansive human-scale view across a large tank excavation: earth-cut basin with gently graded working slopes, many but individually readable adult labourers using simple spades and carrying soil in woven baskets to rising banks, a few timber shade shelters beyond. No finished water body, temples, modern ghats or later palaces; foreground workers convey effort and scale.
uncertainty: Sources disagree on 1697 versus 1707; reign-level date only. Tank attribution is documented; workforce, tools, basin profile and labour organisation are imagined. Do not claim an exact 45-day construction scene.
prompt:
Use case: historical-scene. Asset type: landscape image for the Ahom history website. Create ONE complete landscape scene, approximately 16:9, ideally 3840 x 2160 if available; no collage, inset, labels, border, signature, lettering or watermark. Naturalistic historical illustration with convincing human anatomy, clear purposeful activity, Assam vegetation and humid river-valley light, detailed timber/bamboo/clay surfaces, restrained colour and documentary composition. Avoid theatrical fantasy styling and orange colour cast. References have NARROW roles stated below. Prior generated images provide artistic continuity only, never historical evidence. This is an explicitly interpretive reconstruction; do not pretend uncertainty is known. Ordinary workers have individual Assamese faces and ages, practical plain handwoven wrapped cloth, muted undyed colours, minimal ornament; no royal guards' dress on civilians, no copied famous person. Exact dress and house layouts are creative interpretations, not verified universal Ahom costume. Women wear securely wrapped lower cloth and a modest separate upper drape. No contemporary tailored blouses, zippers, printed cloth or ornamental modern gamosa motifs. No Hindu temple silhouettes in homes or secular workshops, no funerary mound used as a house, no unrelated Tripura architecture. Exclude electricity, asphalt, concrete, steel sheeting, plastic, engines, modern boats, European furniture, factories, colonial uniforms and tea plantations. Keep tools plausible but do not invent technical precision.
